Literal Description

See: The input is a 15x15 grid with a black background containing several single colored pixels (dots) scattered at various positions. Each dot is a different color. The dots' row positions determine how the output grid is partitioned into horizontal bands.

Do: 1. Identify all colored dots in the input grid and record each dot's color and row index. Ignore column positions. 2. Sort the dots by row index from top to bottom. 3. Partition the 15 rows into consecutive bands by computing midpoints between adjacent dots' row indices. The boundary between two adjacent dots at rows r1 and r2 is floor((r1 + r2) / 2) + 1, meaning the first band ends at row floor((r1+r2)/2) and the next band starts at floor((r1+r2)/2)+1. The topmost band starts at row 0 and the bottommost band ends at row 14. 4. For each band, fill it with its dot's color as follows: a. The row where the dot originally sat becomes a full solid horizontal line (all 15 cells filled with the dot's color). b. The first and last rows of the entire grid (row 0 and row 14), if they fall within this band, also become full solid horizontal lines of the dot's color. c. All other rows in the band become border rows: only the leftmost cell (column 0) and rightmost cell (column 14) are filled with the dot's color; the interior cells (columns 1-13) remain black.

Grid: Both input and output grids are 15x15. The background color is black (.). The input contains exactly N single-colored pixels (N varies per puzzle instance) placed at distinct positions. The output uses the full 15x15 grid, partitioned into N horizontal bands with no gaps or overlaps, each rendered as a rectangular frame segment in the corresponding dot's color.

The total number of colored cells in each column is always a perfect square (1, 4, 9, 16, ...).

Do: For each column that contains colored cells, do the following independently: (1) Count the total number of colored cells N in that column. Compute the triangle size as sqrt(N), call it S. (2) Record the colors from top to bottom in the column, preserving their order. (3) Clear the entire column. (4) Build a triangle of S rows at the very bottom of the grid, centered on that column. The bottom row of the triangle sits on the last row of the grid. Row widths from top to bottom are 1, 3, 5, ..., 2S-1 (odd numbers). Each row is horizontally centered on the column. (5) Fill the triangle rows with colors from top (narrowest) to bottom (widest). Assign colors in the same top-to-bottom order as they appeared in the input column: the first color fills cells starting from the top row of the triangle, consuming one cell per triangle position left-to-right, top-to-bottom, until that color's count is exhausted, then continue with the next color. All cells not part of any triangle become black.

Grid: The output grid has the same dimensions as the input grid. The background is entirely black except for the triangle(s) drawn at the bottom. Multiple columns may each produce their own independent triangle, and these triangles coexist on the grid without overlapping.
